newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU officials to discuss French veal demand.
newsitem.headline: EU officials to discuss French veal demand.

text.p: The European Union's beef management committee will on Friday discuss a French demand to suspend an early marketing scheme for calves which it says is ruining the French veal market, EU officials said.
On Tuesday, French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur warned that France might be forced to take unilateral measures to safeguard its market against Dutch veal imports.
Dutch producers receive premiums for their heavier animals and are better able to meet French veal marketing standards.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler told the Farm Council that it was too early to draw conclusions on the impact of the early marketing premium but a review could be brought forward from the planned date in May.
Veal prices were depressed before the early marketing scheme was introduced, he added.
The scheme was approved last October as part of a package to reduce beef and veal production in line with lower consumer demand following the mad cow crisis.
